hot.pointer_line: On now: the last humpbacks and the calmest diving sea of the year, the end of the mwaka clove harvest, Nyerere Day on 14 October, full moons on 26 October and 24 November (party Saturdays 31 Oct and 28 Nov by the venue's rule), and short rains forecast heavier than usual.

items.name: The humpbacks are leaving
items.teaser: Whale season is ending: August and September were the peak, and by November a sighting is luck.
items.story: Humpbacks come north from the Southern Ocean to calve in East African water in the southern winter, and turn back south as it ends. The sources agree on the shape, though not the exact edges. They put the season at roughly June or July to November, with the best odds in July to September, and they name September and October for Nungwi in particular. So early October still gives a fair chance, falling week by week. By November a sighting is luck. Book a dolphin or snorkel trip that might see a whale, not a trip sold as whale-watching.
items.why: In early October a sighting is still possible. By late November it rarely happens.
facts: Peak was Aug-Sep; sightings tail off through Oct and are occasional into Nov
Boats out of Nungwi; also around Mnemba
Go with a dive centre whose skipper keeps distance and cuts the engine rather than chasing

sources.label: Original Diving: Zanzibar overview (humpbacks and sperm whales off Nungwi, Sep-Oct)
Rove.me: humpback whale watching season, Zanzibar

items.name: Between the two winds
items.teaser: The kusi wind drops through October: calm water and good visibility on the north-coast reefs.
items.story: October is the changeover. The southeasterly kusi blows from about June and fades through October. The northeasterly kaskazi does not set in until about December. In between, the sea off the north tip is at its calmest of the year. Dive operators report visibility of 25 m or more in October, and the water warms to around 27 C by early November. This is the window for Leven Bank, a seamount about seven nautical miles off Nungwi with drops from 12 to 55 m and strong currents. It is for advanced divers only. Mnemba is the easier option.
items.why: This is the calmest sea of the year here, and the best time for the deep, current-swept bank.
facts: Oct to Nov; the vuli rains may cloud the water near shore after heavy downpours
Leven Bank is tide-gated: ask the dive desk which day's tide suits it

items.name: Octopus closures: ask at the landing
items.teaser: Villages close reef flats to octopus fishing in turns. No current north-coast closure is published.
items.story: Across Zanzibar, communities close a section of reef flat to octopus fishing for about three months at a time, then reopen it. On Pemba, at Ndooni on Fundo Island, landings on the opening day were more than 20 times a normal day's catch. Not every scheme has held. A 40 km closure in south-east Unguja in 2017 collapsed within weeks because of poaching. A national Octopus Fishery Management Plan for 2026-2030 was validated in June 2025. We found no published list of current closures for Nungwi or Kendwa. Ask at the landing.
items.why: When you buy or order pweza, this explains why some days there is plenty and some days there is none.
facts: Closures rotate by village; no current north-coast closure found in published sources (checked Oct 2026)
Reef flats off the north tip; ask at Nungwi fish landing
Gleaning is busiest on spring low tides around new and full moon

items.name: Two full moons, two party Saturdays
items.teaser: Full moons on Mon 26 Oct and Tue 24 Nov; by the venue's rule, parties on Sat 31 Oct and Sat 28 Nov.
items.story: Full moon is at 04:12 UTC on 26 October, which is 07:12 East Africa Time on Monday 26 October. The next is at 14:53 UTC on 24 November, 17:53 EAT on Tuesday 24 November, and it is a supermoon. Kendwa Rocks says it holds its Full Moon Party on the first Saturday after each full moon. On that rule the parties fall on Saturday 31 October and Saturday 28 November. We could not load the venue's own calendar to confirm this. One third-party guide says the rule is the Saturday closest to the full moon instead, which would make October the 24th. Check before you book a room.
items.why: This decides whether your week is loud or quiet, and what you pay for a room on the party weekend.
facts: Full moon Mon 26 Oct 07:12 EAT; Tue 24 Nov 17:53 EAT. Party (derived): Sat 31 Oct, Sat 28 Nov
Third–party listings give online tickets from TZS 32,000 and TZS 35,000–40,000 at the door (seen Oct 2026); unconfirmed with the venue
Gates around 19:00; arrange the ride back to Nungwi in advance

items.name: Orionids and Leonids
items.teaser: Orionids peak the night of 21-22 Oct, Leonids 17-18 Nov. Both are best after midnight.
items.story: The Orionids, debris from Halley's Comet, peak on the night of 21-22 October. A gibbous moon washes out the evening, but it sets after midnight and leaves the hours before dawn dark, when Orion is high. The Leonids peak on the night of 17-18 November. The moon is a thin crescent that sets early, so the sky stays dark, but expect only about 10 to 15 meteors an hour. Rain may cloud either night. There is no eclipse in this window. The next eclipse is the penumbral lunar eclipse of 20 February 2027, faint even where it can be seen.
items.why: You need no equipment, just a dark stretch of sand facing east, away from the bar lights.
facts: Orionids: night of 21–22 Oct, best pre–dawn. Leonids: night of 17–18 Nov, about 10–15 per hour
Any dark beach; the east-facing side of the point has less light spill
Give your eyes 20 minutes without a phone screen

items.name: The short rains, wetter than usual
items.teaser: The national weather agency forecasts normal to above-normal vuli rains for Unguja, driven by El Nino.
items.story: On 18 August 2026 the Tanzania Meteorological Authority (TMA) issued its October-December forecast. It expects above-normal to normal rainfall on the northern coast, which includes Unguja and Pemba. Onset was forecast for the first and second weeks of October. The rain is expected to get heavier in November and continue into January 2027. The TMA linked this to what it called a very strong El Nino and a warm western Indian Ocean, and it warned of flooding risk. On the coast the short rains usually come as heavy showers, not all-day rain. Expect some lost afternoons and muddy roads.
items.why: Plan an indoor fallback, and leave extra time for the road to Stone Town and the airport.
facts: Onset forecast 1st-2nd week Oct; heavier in Nov, into Jan 2027
Whole island; forecast covers Unguja and Pemba
Check TMA warnings before a long boat day

sources.label: The Chanzo, 19 Aug 2026: TMA raises alarm over very strong El Nino as vuli rains loom

items.name: Last weeks of the main clove harvest
items.teaser: The main mwaka clove crop is picked July to November. In October there is still harvesting to see.
items.story: Zanzibar takes two clove crops a year. The main one is mwaka, from July to November, and its buds are the larger. The smaller vuli crop follows from December to March. The state trading company, ZSTC, has long been the only legal buyer. In October you can still see picking and the mats of buds drying by the road. By late November the main crop is ending, and the rain makes drying harder. If a spice tour is on your list, go early in this window.
items.why: Go in October and you see the harvest being worked, not just a tasting table.
facts: Mwaka harvest Jul-Nov; vuli crop Dec-Mar
Inland estates; Kizimbani is the usual named stop
Name the farm you want and keep to it

items.name: Pweza around the spring tides
items.teaser: Octopus is gathered on foot at low water, so there is most around the spring tides of 26 Oct and 24 Nov.
items.story: Most octopus here is caught by people walking the exposed reef flats at low tide with a spear or stick, often women. The lowest tides come with the spring tides around full and new moon, so landings rise in the days around the full moons of 26 October and 24 November. Pweza is the Swahili word, and the village dish is octopus cooked in coconut curry. Buy it at the landing or eat it where it is cooked. Whether a given reef is open depends on village closures, so some days there is none.
items.why: Eat it in the days around the full moon. Supply depends on the tide, not on a fixed season.
facts: Days around full moon 26 Oct and 24 Nov (and the new moons between)
Nungwi fish landing at low water
Ask whether today's catch is local or brought in

items.name: Nyerere Day, Wednesday 14 October
items.teaser: Mwalimu Nyerere Day is a national public holiday. Offices and banks close; the beach strip carries on.
items.story: On 14 October Tanzania marks the anniversary of the death of Julius Nyerere, the country's first president, who died in London on 14 October 1999. It is a public holiday, with schools, government offices and most businesses closed, and in 2026 it falls on a Wednesday. On the north coast, hotels, bars and boats run as usual. The day mainly affects anything that needs an office: banks, immigration and fisheries permits, government paperwork. Do any of that the day before or after.
items.why: Do not plan bank or office errands for that day.

sources.label: timeanddate.com: Mwalimu Nyerere Day
The Citizen: editorial on Nyerere's legacy

items.name: No festival in October or November
items.teaser: We found no festival in October or November 2026. The big events are in March, June and July.
items.story: We looked for festivals in this window and found nothing we could confirm. Sauti za Busara has moved to March in 2027. The film festival ran in late June 2026. Mwaka Kogwa is in July. Maulid fell in late August this year. One search result listed a Stone Town food festival on 13-16 October, but the article behind it dates from that festival's first edition years ago, so we are not listing it. The next public holiday after Nyerere Day is Independence Day on 9 December, after this window.
items.why: Fewer crowds and lower prices, but nothing scheduled to go to.

sources.label: Edarabia: Tanzania public holidays 2026
The National: first Stone Town food festival (older article, not a 2026 listing)

items.name: Sauti za Busara
items.teaser: The Stone Town festival of African music. In 2027 it is 19-21 March, not the usual February.
items.story: Sauti za Busara ('sounds of wisdom') has run in Stone Town since 2004 and books artists from across Africa and the diaspora, with a strand of Swahili-coast music. The Dhow Countries Music Academy has partnered on that strand. It normally falls in February. For its 24th edition the organisers moved it to 19-21 March 2027, after Ramadan and Eid. From Nungwi, Stone Town is about an hour and a half by road, so most visitors either stay in town for the weekend or take day trips.
items.why: This is the island's main music event and the best time to hear Zanzibari music.
facts: Ticket prices for 2027 not yet published (checked Oct 2026)

items.name: Zanzibar International Film Festival
items.teaser: ZIFF ran 24-28 June 2026, its 29th edition. The 2027 dates have not been announced.
items.story: ZIFF is the island's film festival, held in Stone Town since 1998 with screenings, a parade and evening programmes. The 2026 edition, the 29th, ran 24-28 June. It opened with a parade from the Old Fort to Kisongoni and showed 65 fiction, documentary and animated films under the theme 'AI and the Art of Storytelling'. Recent editions have moved between June and July. We found no 2027 dates, so treat late June to July as likely but unconfirmed.
items.why: If your trip is in June or July, check the festival dates before booking.
facts: Stone Town, Old Fort and other venues

sources.label: The Citizen: ZIFF 2026 spotlights 65 films
ZIFF official site

items.name: Mwaka Kogwa
items.teaser: The Shirazi new-year festival at Makunduchi, in the far south of the island, in July.
items.story: Mwaka Kogwa marks the Shirazi (Persian-derived) new year in Makunduchi, at the southern end of Unguja. It is a community event: a hut is burned to cleanse the year, men stage mock fights with banana stems, and there is singing and food. It falls in July, but the exact day is set locally each year, and we could not find a published date for 2026 or 2027. From the north tip it is a long day trip, about two and a half hours by road each way. Go with a driver who knows the village.
items.why: This is a village festival, not a performance staged for visitors.
facts: July; exact 2027 day not published (checked Oct 2026)
Ask your hotel in June for the confirmed day

sources.label: Pongwe: Zanzibar festivals guide

items.name: Revolution Day and Karume Day
items.teaser: Two holidays specific to Zanzibar: Revolution Day on 12 January and Karume Day on 7 April.
items.story: Zanzibar Revolution Day (Mapinduzi), on 12 January, marks the 1964 revolution. There are official events in Stone Town, and the President of Zanzibar usually gives a speech. In 2027 it falls on a Tuesday. Karume Day, on 7 April, marks the 1972 assassination of Abeid Karume, the first President of Zanzibar. In 2027 it is a Wednesday. On both days offices and banks close, and beach hotels run as usual.
items.why: These are the two dates that will close banks and offices during a winter trip.
facts: Do bank and office errands the day before

sources.label: CalendarLabs: Zanzibar Revolutionary Day
CalendarLabs: Karume Day
Office Holidays: Karume Day 2027

items.name: Ramadan and the two Eids, 2027
items.teaser: Ramadan 2027 is expected to start around 8 February, with Eid al-Fitr around 9 March. Both depend on the moon.
items.story: Ramadan is expected to begin around Monday 8 February 2027, with Eid al-Fitr around Tuesday 9 March. Eid al-Adha is expected around 16-17 May. All three depend on sighting the new moon, and BAKWATA and Zanzibar's Chief Kadhi confirm them only the evening before. During Ramadan, eating, drinking and smoking in public in daylight are best avoided in the villages. Local restaurants may open only after sunset, while beach hotels carry on. Forodhani gardens are busiest after iftar. Eid al-Fitr is a public holiday, normally two days.
items.why: Daytime village life changes for a month. Evenings are busier and more social than usual.
facts: Ramadan ~8 Feb–~8 Mar 2027; Eid al–Fitr ~9 Mar; Eid al–Adha ~16–17 May (all moon–dependent)
Dress more conservatively in the village and keep drinks on the hotel side

items.name: Turtle release day at Mnarani
items.teaser: Each 20 February the Mnarani turtle pond in Nungwi releases the turtles it has been raising into the sea.
items.story: The Mnarani Marine Turtle Conservation Pond is a tidal lagoon near the Nungwi lighthouse. Villagers there raise turtles that local fishers have caught by accident. Each year on 20 February it holds Turtle Release Day, organised by the community with hotels, dive centres and tour operators. In one recent year about 100 turtles went back into the sea. Visitors can attend. Separately, green turtles nest on Zanzibar beaches all year, with a peak in April and May. Hatchlings emerge about 60 days after laying.
items.why: This is the one north-tip event with a fixed date, and it is run by the village itself.
facts: Ask at the pond the week before for the release time

items.name: The two kite winds
items.teaser: The southeasterly kusi blows from June to October and the northeasterly kaskazi from December to March.
items.story: Zanzibar's wind year is two trade winds. The kusi blows from the south-southeast from about May or June to October, mostly at 15 to 20 knots. It is the strong season, and the kite schools at Paje on the east coast are busiest then. The kaskazi blows from the north-east from about December to March. It is lighter, around 12 to 18 knots, and suits beginners. The north tip is sheltered from the kusi, so it has calm water in those months, not good kiting. Experienced riders do kite deep water off Nungwi. Most visitors who kite go to Paje.
items.why: Whether you want wind or calm water decides which coast to stay on and when.
facts: Paje (east coast) for schools; Nungwi for experienced riders

sources.label: We Are Zanzibar: kitesurfing guide
The Kite Spot: kitesurf Paje

listening.name: No listening bar — hear taarab instead
listening.teaser: No vinyl or hi-fi listening bar in Nungwi, Kendwa or Stone Town. The music to hear here is live taarab.
listening.story: We searched for a listening bar, record bar, vinyl bar or dedicated sound-system bar in Nungwi, Kendwa and Stone Town and found nothing as of October 2026. Beach bars play DJs or live bands. For music worth the trip, go to Stone Town for taarab, the Swahili coast's sung poetry with Arab, Indian and African instruments. The Dhow Countries Music Academy, founded in 2002, teaches it and holds weekly evening concerts. Its musicians also play on the rooftop at Emerson on Hurumzi on set nights; one guide says Thursday and Saturday.
listening.why: It saves a wasted search, and taarab is the island's own music.
facts: Dhow Countries Music Academy, Stone Town (sources differ on its current building: Old Customs House, Mizingani, or Vuga; confirm); Emerson on Hurumzi rooftop
DCMA: weekly evening concerts (night unconfirmed). Emerson: dinner from 19:00, taarab on set nights
Emerson's rooftop is reservation-only; call ahead to confirm the music night

notes: WebFetch and direct page loads were blocked for every domain tried (kendwarocks.com, timeanddate.com, busaramusic.org, thechanzo.com, officeholidays.com, wikipedia), so all facts come from search-result extracts of the cited pages, not first-hand page reads. Full Moon Party dates (31 Oct, 28 Nov) are derived from the venue's stated 'first Saturday after the full moon' rule plus published full-moon times; a third-party guide says 'Saturday closest' (would give 24 Oct), and one search extract claimed an 11 Oct 2026 party, which matches no full moon and was discarded. Ticket prices are third-party, unconfirmed; the August board recorded ~50,000 TZS observed. Moon times: 26 Oct 04:12 UTC (Almanac via search); 24 Nov 14:53 UTC (Farmers' Almanac). No eclipse falls in the window; Geminids peak 13-14 Dec, outside it. No current north-coast octopus closure could be identified. Turtle nesting is year-round with an Apr-May peak (national report); nothing site-specific for Nungwi/Kendwa nesting in Oct-Nov was found, so no turtle item on the hot board. Mango peak is contested across sources (Apr/Dec on the old board, Jan in another) - not claimed. Durian timing (November) rests on rove.me plus a traveller blog. A 'Stone Town Food Festival 13-16 Oct 2026' and a 'Zanzibar Beach and Watersports Festival' surfaced only in search summaries traceable to an old article or unsourced text; omitted. Mwaka Kogwa and ZIFF 2027 dates are unpublished. Sauti za Busara 2027 (19-21 Mar) comes from Music In Africa and is consistent with the Ramadan projection; the old board's 'February' line is now wrong for 2027. Emerson on Hurumzi taarab nights (Thu/Sat) are from a single guide; DCMA's current building and concert night are unconfirmed. Maulid 2026 was 25 Aug per holiday listings, settling the August board's open question. Sauti za Busara founding year (2004) and ZIFF founding (1998) are from general knowledge, consistent with ZIFF 2026 being the 29th edition.
